assumptions_and_conventions: Signature(-,+,+,+), spatially flat ds^2=-c^2dt^2+a^2 dx^2. Physical tetrad velocities beta=v/c, e0=c^-1partial_t, ei=a^-1partial_i; a_o=1. Sourceward n; P_n=I-nn^T. Tangent coordinates are ICRS(mu_alpha*cos(delta),mu_delta), not d(alpha)/dt.

Reuse the finite post-decoupling compensated mode: beta_m(a)=b/a, beta_r(a)=-R b, R=3epsilon_m0/(4epsilon_r0); separately conserved positive dust and radiation, optional unperturbed Lambda. Set independent first-order density, metric, shear and lensing perturbations to zero. At every a, epsilon_m beta_m+(4/3)epsilon_r beta_r=a^-4[epsilon_m0-(4/3)epsilon_r0 R]b=0. Quadratic anisotropic stress is outside this approximation.

The physical candidate assumes a source centroid carried by the dust. beta_s=(1+zbar)b at the retarded emission event. Observer beta_o(t)=b/a(t)+ell(t); at t_o, dot(beta_o)=-H0 b+dot(ell). The derivative is in the normal tetrad and is not itself the matter four-acceleration. A nonrotating observer tetrad is chosen; arbitrary catalogue spin is a separate nuisance.

Source-observer proper-time ratio is already used once in the two-ray construction. dot(ell) is a free depth-independent angular acceleration coefficient; in exact FLRW the observer proper acceleration divided by c is dot(ell)+H0 ell. Real local metric/solar-system effects are not thereby modeled; their common dipole can be absorbed but remaining spatial/time terms are unknown.

The physical theorem is local at first order and at true background depths. The finite retained-row experiment fixes reported Quaia redshifts/directions. Photometric-redshift errors, catastrophe law, selection, source intrinsic motion and nonlinear physical remainder are not supplied by this plug-in design.

The quantitative velocity requirement is max(|b|/a_i,R|b|,|b+ell|)<<1, plus Doppler displacement small relative to the distance-redshift variation scale. It is a validity condition, not a prior. No finite remainder or nonzero interval of certified physical accuracy is established.

constructive_derivation.retarded_clock: To zeroth order dt_s/dt_o=a_s/a_o. Since dx_s/dt_s=c beta_s/a_s, its displacement per observer time is c beta_s/a_o. Likewise observer displacement is c beta_o/a_o. Differentiating the sourceward unit direction gives P_n c(beta_s-beta_o)/(a_o chi). First-order aberration adds P_n dot(beta_o). Source proper-time and cosmic-time differences are quadratic in velocities in this unperturbed metric. Adding a further1/(1+z) to the source term would double-count the clock conversion.
constructive_derivation.physical_response: mu_rad_per_time(n,zbar)=P_n{H0 k_b(zbar)b+H0 k_ell(zbar)ell+dot(ell)}+r_mu; I(z)=H0 chi(z)/c=integral_0^z du/E(u), k_b=z/I-1, k_ell=-1/I. The b column is a history response distinct from local observer velocity and the free common glide. r_mu is an unbounded physical/source/processing remainder here, never zero-filled for admission.
constructive_derivation.curl_and_acceleration: At each fixed true depth the displayed vector field is grad_S2[n dot constant], hence pure E1 and curl-free. The homogeneous dust is geodesic and spatially irrotational at this order. No omega/cosmic-curl or matter-four-acceleration response follows. A depth-dependent sample mask can mix fitted E/B coefficients; it does not alter the physical fixed-depth statement.
constructive_derivation.closed_background: Freeze the already evaluated synthetic background r=Omega_r=1/10000,Omega_m=1-r,Omega_Lambda=Omega_k=0,H0=70km/s/Mpc. E(z)=(1+z)^(3/2)*sqrt(1+r z). Put Q=sqrt((1+z)(1+r z)). Then I=2z/(1+z+Q), k_b=(z-1+Q)/2, k_ell=-(1+z+Q)/(2z). For stable evaluation use k_b=z/2*[1+(1+r+r z)/(Q+1)]. These are scalar closed forms; no quadrature or ODE is needed.
constructive_derivation.units: Let K_H=H0*(Julian_year_seconds)*(microarcseconds_per_radian), with1Julianyear=31557600s,1au=149597870700m,1pc=(648000/pi)au. For H0=70km/s/Mpc,K_H=14.76646685987891microas/yr. Define fit amplitudes a_b=K_H b and a_ell=K_H ell in microas/yr. Mean row is E_i[k_b a_b+k_ell a_ell+g], with g=dot(ell) converted to microas/yr, free and unconstrained. E_i rows are east_i^T,north_i^T. The scalar profiles are dimensionless.
constructive_derivation.null_limits: b=ell=dot(ell)=0 gives zero displayed PM. A source and observer sharing decaying dust do not generally give zero because they sample different emission times. With constant H, I=z and k_b=0 exactly. Near z=0, k_b=Eprime(0)z/2+O(z^2)=(3+r)z/4+O(z^2), while k_ell=-1/z-(3+r)/4+O(z). The local-velocity singularity requires z>0 and the finite-amplitude Doppler smallness condition. r->0 is the EdS scalar-control limit, not an admissible nonzero compensated-radiation history at r=0.

identification_lemmas.three_depth_theorem: For0<z1<z2<z3 and strictly concave positive I on[z1,z3], the3x3 profile matrix with rows[k_b(zj),k_ell(zj),1] is nonsingular. Multiply rowj byI_j, then add column3 to column1: the resulting rows are[zj,-1,I_j], with determinant equal to det(rows[1,zj,I_j]). Therefore det(profile)=det([1,z,I])/product(I_j). Strict concavity makes the latter negative for ordered depths, hence nonzero. Iprime=1/E and Isecond=-Eprime/E^2<0 when Eprime>0. Thus history, local velocity and common glide are distinguishable in the ideal angular/depth design. Cartesian three-component separation additionally requires sufficient angular support. The actual retained sample and added nuisance span must be tested numerically; this is not an empirical rank claim.
identification_lemmas.frame_quotient_theorem: For fixed retained rows/design/weights, let L be any linear contrast with L U=0. If the catalogue differs from ideal tangent PM by U c(y) for any possibly data-dependent coefficient vector, then L[y+U c(y)]=Ly pointwise. In particular if U includes global B1 and common E1, any additive global spin and common glide vanish. Spin coefficients may have been estimated using other sources; that does not change the result. For an operator T=I+B A,LB=0 implies L T=L for everyA. Full-sky E/B orthogonality is unnecessary. This does not cover source-dependent or time-dependent calibration outsidecol(U), changes of selected rows/weights, finite coordinate rotations without consistent basis transport, or a general NNR operator.
identification_lemmas.gaia_consequence: Gaia AppendixE qualifies the pure global rotation correction component. The proposed U includes all three binwise B1 triplets, hence global B1, and a common E1 triplet; it removes that component and the free observer glide under the fixed-design model. This narrows the previous undifferentiated frame/glide blocker. It does not establish source selection, residual spatial covariance or full detector calibration.
identification_lemmas.radio_countercondition: For radio sourcei with session slope functional ell_i and session spin c(t), correction to its fitted slope can be B_i ell_i[c(t)]. Different source epochs/weights and the five underlying solutions need not share ell_i[c(t)]. Thus even instantaneous rotational corrections can become source-dependent final PM corrections. A single common B1 quotient cannot be assumed to annihilate these. The actual radio NNR/time-series transfer remains HOLD; radio is excluded from the proposed new Gaia-only fit.
identification_lemmas.old_contrasts_relation: The six R23-Q low-minus-high and middle-minus-high E1 contrasts already remove a truly common E1 amplitude. The continuously varying profiles k_b,k_ell are not generally in the18 piecewise-constant E1/B1 span. Substituting bin-centre or unweighted bin-average kernels into old coefficients would not be the new retained-row estimator. Its exact weighted response requires new cross-moments.

import json,sys,math
import sympy as s
z,r=s.symbols('z r', positive=True)
y=1+z
q=s.sqrt(y*(1+r*z))
I=2*z/(y+q)
kb=(z-1+q)/2
kb_stable=z*(1+(1+r+r*z)/(q+1))/2
kl=-(y+q)/(2*z)
E=y**s.Rational(3,2)*s.sqrt(1+r*z)
res={
 'kernel_from_distance':s.simplify(kb-(z/I-1)),
 'local_kernel':s.simplify(kl+1/I),
 'stable_kernel':s.simplify(kb-kb_stable),
 'distance_derivative':s.simplify(s.diff(I,z)-1/E),
 'low_z_coefficient':s.simplify(s.limit(kb/z,z,0)-(3+r)/4),
 'dust_limit':s.simplify(kb.subs(r,0)-(z+s.sqrt(1+z)-1)/2),
 'constant_H_history_null':s.simplify(z/z-1),
}
zs=[s.Rational(5,4),s.Integer(3),s.Rational(21,4)]
D=s.Matrix([[kb.subs({z:v,r:0}),kl.subs({z:v,r:0}),1] for v in zs]).det()
# Generic column operation check, independent of any distance law.
z1,z2,z3,I1,I2,I3=s.symbols('z1 z2 z3 I1 I2 I3',positive=True)

# Units: 1 Julian year=31557600 s, IAU parsec=648000/pi au, au=149597870700 m.
pc_m=648000/math.pi*149597870700
KH=70000/(1e6*pc_m)*31557600*(180/math.pi)*3600*1e6
